_about: Lines the game itself writes, outside the storylets: what the monitor says about a person's ordinary day (comings and goings), an empty doorstep at the usual hour, gossip about people in the subject's world, and deliveries. Placeholders as in the storylets: {A} the subject, {B} the other person in view, {C} someone talked about who isn't there, {place} where it happens, {seen} a real count of sightings, {when} a day name, {sender} and {look} for a parcel. The same rules apply: only what is seen or heard, no thoughts, names only from a name in the line.

leave: {A} steps out of {place} and looks up and down the street.
enter: {A} goes in at {place}. The door slides shut.
{A} goes through {place} without a look back.
enterSeen: {A} goes in at {place}: the same door, {seen} days on the feed.
Same door as before, {place}. Seen going in here on {seen} days.
seat: {A} sits down at {place} and stays put.
stand: {A} stops at {place} and stands a while.
{A} finds a spot at {place} and waits there.
queue: {A} gets in line at {place}, reading the board.
keeper: {A} takes the counter at {place} and ties an apron on.
{A} sets up behind the counter at {place}.
eat: {A} eats slowly and watches the street.
chat: {A} and {B.desc} trade a few words at {place}.
smalltalk: Overheard: {B.desc} says the lift was slow again this morning.
Overheard: {A} says the rain is meant to come back tonight.
Overheard: {B.desc} says the broth here was better last year.
Overheard: {A} says the new stall on the corner runs out by eight.
Overheard: {B.desc} asks if {A} heard the sirens last night.
metro: {A} heads up to the metro platform.
{A} takes the lift up to the platform.
metroOff: {A} steps off the lift from the trains.

first: The door stays shut. Seen opening near this hour on {seen} days before.
No sign of {A} at the door. Out by now on {seen} days before.
later: No movement at the door. The window stays dark.

sick: Overheard: {B} says {C.first} has been out sick since {when}.
Overheard: {B} mentions {C.first} is down with a fever. Hasn't left the apartment.
Overheard: {B} says someone should bring {C.first} soup. "Sick since {when}, poor thing."
parcel: Overheard: {B} says a drone came for {C.first} {when}. "It was {look}, from {sender}."
Overheard: {B} mentions {C.first} got a delivery {when}. "From {sender}, if you can believe it."
Overheard: {B} says {C.first} had something from {sender} come {when}.

sick: Down with a fever since {when}, per {S} (overheard).

arrive: A delivery drone settles at the door and waits.
A drone drops to the doorstep and hovers, parcel strapped on.
A delivery drone comes in low and holds at the door.
take: The door opens. {A} takes the parcel from the drone.
{A} comes to the door and lifts the parcel off the drone.
{A} steps out, signs with a thumb, and takes the parcel.
label: Label on the box: {A.full}. Printed under it: {sender}.
Shipping tag, face up: {A.full}, from {sender}.
The label reads {A.full}. Sender: {sender}.
nobody: Nobody comes to the door. The drone sets the parcel on the step and leaves.
The drone waits, then lowers the parcel onto the step and goes.

silent: {A} turns the box over once and goes back in.
{A} pulls the cardigan tighter and goes back in with the box.

Phone, one side: {A} says: "The pharmacy sent it. I'll take it now. Yes, with food."
